topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, contextualizes cancer evolution within the broader course, and outlines the expected learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Regulation in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how genetic driver mutations and epigenetic alterations independently drive clonal fitness, phenotypic changes, and cancer progression.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cells
topics.groupedBecause: They explore tissue hierarchies and evaluate experimental evidence from leukemia and colorectal cancer demonstrating how cancer stem cells drive tumor initiation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Promotion and Inflammatory Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how external environmental exposures and chronic inflammation act as promotional stimuli to enable mutated tissues to advance toward malignancy.

topics.label: Established Tumor Microenvironment, Profiling Methods, and Coevolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the dependency of established tumors on supportive stroma, outline modern spatial profiling methods, and synthesize the coevolutionary factors driving cancer progression.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
